(Capacity: 18,119) |champion=AAC regular season and [[2025 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|tournament]] champions |tourney=[[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result =First Round }} {{2024–25 American Athletic Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Memphis]] in the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Tigers, led by seventh-year head coach [[Penny Hardaway]], played their home games at [[FedExForum]] as members of the [[American Conference (NCAA)|American Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 29–6, 16–2 in AAC play to win the conference championship. They defeated [[2024–25 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]], [[2024–25 Tulane Green Wave men's basketball team|Tulane]], and [[2024–25 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] to win the [[2025 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 5 seed in the West region. There they were upset in the first round by [[2024–25 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]]. ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 22–10, 11–7 in AAC play, to finish in a tie for fifth place.
